PFAI.Influence.WeaknessesInfo: A soft spot the party can exploit once they find it. Putting it in play LOWERS every influence DC — by 2 for a minor one, 5 for a major one. Example: she is vain about her family name, so praise aimed at the name lands harder than praise aimed at her.
PFAI.Influence.ResistancesInfo: Something about this person that makes them harder to sway. Putting it in play RAISES every influence DC — by 2 for a minor one, 5 for a strong one. Example: she will not discuss anything that could be overheard.
PFAI.Influence.PenaltiesInfo: A blunder the party can commit. Putting it in play RAISES every influence DC — by 2 for a minor slip, 5 for a serious one. Unlike a resistance this is something the party did, not something they are up against. Example: naming the Chelish attaché aloud.
PFAI.Influence.ThresholdsInfo: Influence point totals that buy a concession, ascending. When the party's total reaches one, it reveals itself and the NPC does what it says. The last one is what a full success looks like.
PFAI.Influence.TraitDescriptionHint: Read aloud once the party discovers it.

PFAI.Research.RemainingHint: Research points still obtainable across every source. If this drops below what the remaining findings need, the research has become unwinnable — open another source.
PFAI.Research.SourcesInfo: Places and people the party can work. Each yields only so many research points, which is what stops them grinding one shelf forever. A source at its cap is exhausted and offers nothing further.
PFAI.Research.SourceCapTooltip: Taken from this source / its cap

PFAI.Research.FindingsInfo: Research point totals that yield something specific, ascending. Crucial clues should cost fewer points than lavish rewards. The last one is what finishing the job looks like.
PFAI.Research.ComplicationsInfo: Interruptions to the work. Each fires either at a research point total or after so much time has passed. One carrying a DC shift makes the rest of the research harder or easier once it is in play.
PFAI.Research.SourceCapped: “{name}” reached its cap; only part of that roll counted.

PFAI.Research.BecauseProgress: the party has already found {points} research points and knows more than they did
PFAI.Research.DeleteConfirm: Permanently delete “{name}”? This cannot be undone.
PFAI.Info.GmNotes: Your own notes. Players never see this, whatever their permissions — it is the one place safe for spoilers, pacing reminders and twists.
PFAI.Info.Participants: Who is taking part. Each row rolls for itself: pick a check and press the die. A player only sees roll controls for actors they own. Drag actors in from the sidebar, or use the button above.
PFAI.Info.Round: One round is one pass around the table: every participant may act once. Next Round advances the count and clears everyone's acted mark.
PFAI.Info.BaseDC: The difficulty anchor you chose. Every generated check is this number plus an adjustment, so raising it makes the whole thing harder at once. Editing it does not retune checks that already exist.
PFAI.Info.ChasePremise: What you read to the table: who is chasing whom, why, and what happens if they fail. Written by you and kept word for word — the AI builds obstacles from it but never rewrites it.
PFAI.Info.Obstacles: The sequence the party runs. Each needs a number of chase points to clear: success 1, critical success 2, critical failure −1. Only one is shown at a time; players see the active one, and you can browse the rest with the arrows.
PFAI.Info.ObstacleRounds: How long the party may spend on this obstacle before you call it. Not a published rule — the rules let rounds run until an obstacle is cleared — so treat it as a pacing aid.
PFAI.Info.ChasePoints: Progress on this obstacle. Cleared when it reaches the goal, which comes from party size: half the obstacles need one fewer than the party, half need two fewer.
PFAI.Info.WhoTheyAre: The person you are trying to win over, as you described them, plus the Perception and Will the published stat block asks for. The slider edits those numbers.
PFAI.Info.InfluenceSituation: Where this conversation happens and what is at stake. Yours, kept word for word.
PFAI.Info.Discovery: Checks that reveal rather than score. A success uncovers the cheapest thing still hidden — the easiest approach first, then a soft spot, then a resistance — and a critical success uncovers two. They earn no influence points.
PFAI.Info.InfluenceSkills: Checks that score. Success earns 1 influence point, critical success 2, critical failure costs 1. Only revealed approaches can be rolled; reveal one with the eye to put it in play.
PFAI.Info.ResearchTopic: The question the party is trying to answer. Yours, kept word for word — the AI works out where they can dig, but not what they are digging for.
PFAI.Info.ResearchSituation: Where the work happens and what pressure is on it: a deadline, a rival, a suspicious archivist.
PFAI.Info.ResearchPoints: Total found across every source. Findings unlock as this rises, and complications can fire from it.

PFAI.Info.InfiltrationTarget: The place or organisation being broken into, as you described it. Yours, kept word for word.
PFAI.Info.InfiltrationSituation: When this happens and what cover the party has — a festival, a shift change, a storm.
PFAI.Info.Awareness: How close they are to being caught. A failed check adds 1, a critical failure 2, and the end of every round adds 1 more. Unlike the other subsystems a failure costs no progress — it costs secrecy.
PFAI.Info.EdgePoints: Advantages bought by planning ahead. Spend one to treat a failed check as a success and take back the awareness it drew. Earned from the preparations below.
PFAI.Info.Objectives: The stages of the job: get inside, reach the vault, get out. Each holds obstacles, and each obstacle needs infiltration points — success 1, critical success 2. Failure earns none and raises awareness instead.
PFAI.Info.IndividualObstacle: Every character has to get past this one themselves — slipping by a guard, say — rather than the party clearing it together.
PFAI.Info.Breakpoints: What being noticed costs. Once awareness passes one it fires for good, usually raising every DC from then on. Only the highest one passed applies, not the sum.
PFAI.Info.InfiltrationComplications: Problems that stop everything until dealt with. While one is active it is the only thing the party can roll against. They fire at an awareness total, after so many rounds, or when you call for it.
PFAI.Info.Opportunities: Optional risks that pay off in something other than progress: a password overheard, a guard's rota copied. Taking one is never required.
PFAI.Info.Preparations: What the party can do before the job to earn edge points. Each is offered once. Mark it with + when it succeeds to award the point, or × to record the attempt without one.
PFAI.Info.InfiltrationRound: One round is one pass around the table. Advancing a round also raises awareness on its own, which is what makes lingering dangerous.

PFAI.Infiltration.AwarenessPerRoundHint: Added at the end of each round
